result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B explains why both extremes fail. It recommends checking a field when the person leaves it, using 'touched' state, and adds stale-response handling for the username check. A makes submit the default instead of checking on leaving a field, and it doesn't explain why submit-only validation fails, so it mostly sides with the designer. Both answer the username and password cases well and give concrete behavior for each field. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer A recommends validating when the person leaves a field, using a 'touched' rule so untouched fields show no errors, and re-checking live once an error is showing. It also explains the problems with both extremes, including the drawbacks of waiting until submit. Answer B is strong on field details and adds useful extras like input attributes and keeping the button pressable, but it defaults to submit-time validation for email. That means it misses blur-based checking and does not really deal with errors piling up at submit.
